config.title: Build heartbeat and presence client logic

intro.title: Build heartbeat and presence client logic
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a client-side heartbeat and presence system for a web application. You will learn to use JavaScript's setInterval and clearInterval functions to send periodic signals (heartbeats) to a server, indicating that a user is active and online. The core programming concept involves managing state and side effects to track user presence over time. You will implement this by creating a function that starts a timer to send heartbeat requests and another to stop it, using fetch for network communication. This will help you understand how real-time applications maintain live user status updates.
intro.usecase: Heartbeat and presence logic is essential for any application that needs to track user activity and connection status in real-time. For example, collaborative tools like Google Docs or Figma use it to show live cursors and avatars of other active users, while chat applications like Slack or Discord display online/offline status indicators. As a developer, implementing this pattern is key for building interactive dashboards, multiplayer games, or live support systems where knowing who is connected and active directly impacts the user experience.

objectives: Implement a heartbeat function that periodically sends status updates to a server
Initialize a presence tracking state to monitor user activity status
Configure event listeners to detect user presence changes (active/idle/away)
Construct a client-side presence manager that coordinates heartbeat and status updates
Integrate presence logic with a simulated server API to send and receive status data
Manipulate the DOM to display real-time user presence status based on activity
Control the heartbeat interval and manage cleanup to prevent memory leaks

steps.instruction: Import the EventEmitter class from the 'events' module to handle event-driven communication.

successCriteria: EventEmitter is imported from the 'events' module.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Create the PresenceClient class structure
steps.instruction: Create a class named PresenceClient with a constructor that accepts a userId parameter.
steps.hint: Use the class keyword followed by the class name, then define a constructor method that takes userId as a parameter.
steps.expectedOutcome: A PresenceClient class is defined with a constructor that can receive a userId.
successCriteria: The PresenceClient class exists and has a constructor method that accepts userId as a parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've defined both the class and a constructor method that takes a userId parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a class named PresenceClient with a constructor that accepts a userId parameter.

steps.title: Initialize class properties in the constructor
steps.instruction: Inside the PresenceClient constructor, initialize the following properties: userId, isOnline (set to false), lastSeen (set to current timestamp), and create a new EventEmitter instance assigned to a property named emitter.
steps.hint: Use 'this.propertyName = value' syntax to assign each property. For lastSeen, use Date.now(). For the EventEmitter, create a new instance with 'new EventEmitter()'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The constructor now properly sets up the initial state and event emitter for the presence client.
successCriteria: The PresenceClient constructor initializes userId, isOnline (false), lastSeen (Date.now()), and creates an EventEmitter instance assigned to emitter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've initialized some properties, but not all required ones. Make sure to set userId, isOnline (to false), lastSeen (to Date.now()), and create an EventEmitter instance.
steps.feedbackWrong: The constructor doesn't contain the required property initializations. Review the instruction and add all four properties: userId, isOnline, lastSeen, and emitter.

steps.title: Add the startHeartbeat method
steps.instruction: Inside the PresenceClient class, add a method named startHeartbeat that sets up a setInterval to update the lastSeen property every 5 seconds.
steps.hint: The method should use setInterval to run a function that updates this.lastSeen with the current timestamp (Date.now()).
steps.expectedOutcome: The PresenceClient class will have a startHeartbeat method that periodically updates the lastSeen timestamp.
successCriteria: The startHeartbeat method is defined in the PresenceClient class and uses setInterval to update this.lastSeen every 5000 milliseconds.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a method, but check that it uses setInterval to update this.lastSeen every 5 seconds (5000 milliseconds).
steps.feedbackWrong: The startHeartbeat method is missing or doesn't properly set up the interval to update lastSeen. Review the method implementation.

steps.title: Add the stopHeartbeat method
steps.instruction: Add a stopHeartbeat method to the PresenceClient class that clears the interval if it exists.
steps.hint: Check if this.heartbeatInterval is defined, then clear it and set it to null.
steps.expectedOutcome: The PresenceClient class now has a stopHeartbeat method that safely clears any active heartbeat interval.
successCriteria: The stopHeartbeat method is defined, checks if this.heartbeatInterval exists, clears it, and sets it to null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a method, but make sure it checks if the interval exists before clearing it and resets the property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The stopHeartbeat method is missing or doesn't properly clear the interval.

steps.title: Implement the goOffline method
steps.instruction: Add a goOffline method to the PresenceClient class that sets isOnline to false, stops the heartbeat, and emits an 'offline' event.
steps.hint: Inside the class, define a method named goOffline. Set this.isOnline to false, call this.stopHeartbeat(), and emit an 'offline' event using this.emit('offline').
steps.expectedOutcome: The PresenceClient class will have a goOffline method that handles disconnection by updating state, stopping the heartbeat, and emitting an event.
successCriteria: The goOffline method is defined, sets isOnline to false, calls stopHeartbeat, and emits an 'offline' event.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added the method, but check if it sets isOnline to false, calls stopHeartbeat, and emits the 'offline' event.
steps.feedbackWrong: The goOffline method is missing or incomplete. Ensure it updates isOnline, stops the heartbeat, and emits an event.

steps.title: Add the getStatus method
steps.instruction: Create a getStatus method inside the PresenceClient class that returns an object with userId, isOnline, and lastSeen properties.
steps.hint: Add a method named getStatus that returns an object containing the current user ID, online status, and last seen timestamp.
steps.expectedOutcome: The PresenceClient class will have a getStatus method that returns an object with the user's current presence status.
successCriteria: A getStatus method is defined in the PresenceClient class and returns an object containing userId, isOnline, and lastSeen properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a method, but make sure it returns an object with exactly userId, isOnline, and lastSeen properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The getStatus method is missing or doesn't return the required object structure. Check the method name and return value.

steps.title: Create a helper function to simulate network activity
steps.instruction: Create a function named simulateNetworkActivity that takes a PresenceClient instance as a parameter and randomly calls either goOnline or goOffline on it.
steps.hint: Use Math.random() to generate a random number between 0 and 1, then call goOnline() if the number is less than 0.5, otherwise call goOffline().
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a simulateNetworkActivity function that can test the presence client's online/offline behavior with random simulation.
successCriteria: The simulateNetworkActivity function exists, takes a client parameter, and randomly calls goOnline or goOffline on that client.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function takes a client parameter and uses Math.random() to decide whether to call goOnline() or goOffline().
steps.feedbackWrong: The function is missing or doesn't properly simulate random network activity. Review the instructions and try again.
